newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate stays high after choppy session.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate stays high after choppy session.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate stayed high on Monday after a choppy session, triggered by a liquidity squeeze, dealers said.
The overnight was done between 13 and 20 percent, they said.
It traded as high as 25 percent on Friday as a tight squeeze for ringgit-funds at the short end of the market caused players to scramble for overnight money.
"The overnight will remain above 10 percent in the next few days unless Bank Negara does something to ease the market," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.
Bank Negara said in a statement on Friday that the rise in money market rates was a temporary phenomenon.
It also said that its monetary policy stance remains unchanged.

The rise in interbank rates started on Thursday after Bank Negara intervened aggressively in the foreign exchange market to stem the slide of the ringgit. The central bank was said to have sold around $1 billion.
The intervention drained liquidity from the system, causing the market to be short and interbank rates to rise to unusually high levels.
Earlier, interbank rates were generally lower compared with Friday's levels.
One-, two- and three-week money were at 8.0/9.5 percent against 10.0/20.0 percent on Friday.
One- to six-month money fell to 7.5/8.0 percent from 8.5/9.0 percent.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were generally higher.
Futures market dealers said players, who earlier sold because of uncertainty in interest rate direction, were covering back their positions.
Trading, however, was cautious ahead of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on Tuesday, they said.
At 0900 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was up three points to 92.53, or an implied yield of 7.47 percent.
September rose one to 92.53, or 7.47 percent.
